body:
### What's wrong

tcp/udp, ipv4, port-forwarding, holepunching, ipv6, nat, firewalls (of ISP), etc, are trash. 
ISP business is close to a monopoly of a few players in every country. They sometimes throttle torent traffic, etc. "Net neutrality" is not a thing.
Dead internet theory is legit. The internet we see is curated by the big players, who pay the ISPs big money to make their services less throttled than the competition. Services can get blocked and banned on national scale, by world governments. ISPs can shut down internet of a whole city, to prevent protests or even cheatings in exams lol. 
Nobody spins up a minecraft server to play with their friends anymore, because firstly port-forwarding on their routers is often locked/forbidden, ipv4 addresses are limited, and ISPs don't want customers to be running servers, etc. Instead, kids are stuck watching streams of others playing the game. 
VPNs, VPS, even Tor, are all inferior solutions, like fragile ductaping on top of a broken system.

### Solution 

People have routers, people have antennas, so they should be able to connect up to make their own free internet.

Time for the world to switch to Reticulum. It is like meshcore or meshtastic, but it's just a packet-routing protocol, so it supports ethernet, fibre, wifi, lora radio antennas, bluetooth, anything! People can lay the wiring themselves, or spin up radios, and so connect with neighbours, and so on. No ISP needed. And "destination" is a public-key hash, and not just a dumb ip addresss which anyone could spoof. Routing is done by Transport nodes which listen for "announce" messages, and store the first (thus closest) peer who announced the said destination. And so, it's possible to trasmit messages over multiple hops.

### Feature Request

If you clone tox repo and replace ip-addresses with "destinations" and tcp/udp with their Reticulum transport protocol, it should work! Voice, video, text, over Tox over Reticulum, all on a p2p mesh net, no ISP needed! OMG so cool! Also, Reticulum's coverage is growing daily. 

https://reticulum.network/manual/understanding.html
This is the main dev in charge: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pnyuSWy66cI
title: [FR]: Tox over Reticulum mesh network (no ISP needed)
